title: Systems Biology
tagline: Kinetic models, gene-expression dynamics, network motifs, switches and oscillators, noise, robustness, metabolic networks, pattern formation and fitting models to data
summary: Systems biology asks how the behaviour of cells emerges from networks of interacting molecules, and answers with mathematical models. This course builds dynamical models of gene expression, the network motifs that recur in nature, switches, oscillators and noise, signalling and robust adaptation, metabolic networks and pattern formation, and the statistics of fitting models to data.

chapters.title: Modelling biological systems
chapters.summary: Why we model, kinetic equations, mass action and steady states.

chapters.title: Dynamics of gene expression
chapters.summary: Production and degradation, response times, Hill functions and autoregulation.

chapters.title: Network motifs
chapters.summary: Feed-forward loops, negative and positive feedback, and the design principles of transcription networks.

chapters.title: Switches and oscillators
chapters.summary: Bistability and hysteresis, the genetic toggle switch, the repressilator and circadian clocks.

chapters.title: Noise in gene expression
chapters.summary: Stochastic chemical kinetics, the Gillespie algorithm and the consequences of noise for cells.

chapters.title: Signalling, adaptation and robustness
chapters.summary: Bacterial chemotaxis, exact adaptation, ultrasensitivity and robust design.

chapters.title: Metabolic networks
chapters.summary: Stoichiometric models, flux balance analysis and metabolic control analysis.

chapters.title: Pattern formation
chapters.summary: Morphogen gradients, Turing patterns and reaction–diffusion in development.

chapters.title: Fitting models to data
chapters.summary: Parameter estimation, identifiability and choosing between competing models.
